nodes.name: Error Trigger
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: typeVersion. Atlas: an error workflow must start with an Error Trigger, is chosen in the main workflow's Workflow Settings, and one error workflow can serve many workflows; the Error Trigger page says the error workflow must be published and cannot be tested with a manual run (read from the documentation, not seen on a real n8n).

nodes.name: Build message
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: typeVersion, the 'assignments' shape and the exact field paths. Atlas: the payload holds execution id and url, error message and stack, last node, mode, workflow id and name; execution id and url are missing when the trigger node itself failed; retryOf is present only on retries. Do not add the request body or any header to the message.

nodes.name: Notify placeholder
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: the node type name and typeVersion. Replace this node with the client's chat or e-mail node and send {{ $json.message }}. What lands here by design, because a person must look: a missing business id or document text; a 401, 409, 400 or 413 from the trigger endpoint; and a 503 (busy) in every round of the main workflow's wait-and-sign-again loop, which means the event was NOT accepted.
